rec.name: Homepage-Only Desktop Navigation (Header Menu Override)
rec.status: Built — in development theme, awaiting client feedback

what.text: A header setting that lets you assign a different navigation menu to the homepage on desktop only. All other pages and mobile keep the normal main menu. The header section has a new 'Homepage menu' dropdown that lists the store's existing menus.

why.text: The homepage has a different job from inner pages. On desktop, a slimmed-down or differently prioritised menu cuts distraction and steers visitors toward the hero, category tiles and key collections. A full main menu can compete with those. Page-specific navigation also lets you A/B test menu structure and labels on the highest-traffic entry page without touching the global menu. The ticket does not state the goal, so this reasoning is inferred.

how.text: 1) In the header section schema, add a 'link_list' setting called 'Homepage menu'. 2) In header Liquid, check whether the current template is the homepage (template.name == 'index') and the viewport is desktop. If so, render the homepage menu. Otherwise render the standard 'Menu' setting. 3) Do the desktop-only split with a separate desktop nav block hidden on mobile via CSS, or a media-query wrapper. Mobile keeps the drawer built from the main menu. 4) Fall back to the main menu if no homepage menu is selected. 5) In the theme editor, create or choose the menu in Shopify Navigation, then select it in Header > Homepage menu. The ticket says integration is 'very simple': one extra input field. The fallback and the desktop/mobile split are inferred.

items: Header > 'Homepage menu': dropdown of existing Shopify menus (the screenshot shows 'Rechtliches' selected)
Existing header settings stay unchanged: Menu (main menu), Secondary menu, desktop and mobile logo and width, Custom CSS
Applies to the Homepage template on Desktop only

dependencies.text: A Shopify theme with a header section that has a link_list setting. A menu must exist under Online Store > Navigation for the homepage. No apps are needed. The ticket reports it built in the 'goldkindchen/main [Development]' theme. The dropdown label is English ('Homepage menu') while the other labels are German, so the theme has a mixed-language editor.

items: Homepage click-through rate on nav items vs. hero and category tiles
Homepage bounce rate and exit rate
Sessions per visitor and conversion rate for desktop homepage entrants
Search-icon usage (to check the slimmer menu isn't hurting discoverability)
